limitations: The selected children supply distinct activated and triggered criteria; their structural links are not invented direct citations.
No real ability-kind detection or mana-ability classifier is supplied.
rule.paraphrase: Mana abilities form a rules-defined subset of activated and triggered abilities. Membership requires the applicable complete criteria set, while other generated effects and additional timing restrictions do not by themselves disqualify a qualifying ability.
rule.topic: Two criteria families determine mana-ability membership

limitations: Both numbered external criteria dependencies remain unprojected.
The criteria are descriptive evidence; no targeting, loyalty, library, replacement, or output evaluation occurs.
rule.paraphrase: An activated ability qualifies only when it has no target, could supply mana on resolution, is not a loyalty ability, and neither its payment requirements nor its effect transfers a card into or out of a library. Evaluate these criteria with self-replacement effects considered and other applicable replacement effects disregarded.
rule.topic: Activated-mana criteria and the replacement-effect distinction

limitations: The selected activated criterion is represented, while the targeting dependency remains unresolved.
No event detection, trigger matching, triggered ability execution, or mana output calculation occurs.
rule.paraphrase: A triggered ability qualifies when it has no target, could supply mana on resolution, and its trigger is tied to activating or resolving an activated mana ability, or to mana entering a player's pool. The activated-mana criterion is supplied by the selected activated classification rule.
rule.topic: Triggered-mana criteria require a qualifying trigger relationship

limitations: Current output and activation eligibility are distinctions, not evaluated results.
The source example contributes only to the verified block span and digest; no example text is retained.
rule.paraphrase: A qualifying mana ability keeps that classification when the current state prevents it from generating mana. Membership in the rule category is separate from present activation eligibility and from the output a particular use could produce.
rule.topic: Classification persists independently of present mana output

limitations: The ordinary activation procedure remains an unresolved large subsystem.
Selected exception coverage does not supply general activation or payment semantics.
rule.paraphrase: Using an activated mana ability depends on the ordinary activated-ability procedure, with the selected descendants describing special opportunities, immediate behavior, and a restriction on repeating the same activation.
rule.topic: Activated-mana procedure retains a general activation dependency

limitations: These opportunity categories neither grant real permission nor decide current activation eligibility.
Priority, casting, ability procedures, resolution, and payment are not implemented.
rule.paraphrase: Activated mana abilities have opportunities tied to priority, spell or ability procedures requiring mana, and a rule's or effect's request for mana payment. A qualifying request may arise during an ongoing spell or ability procedure, including its resolution.
rule.topic: Special opportunities to activate a mana ability

limitations: The explicit stack-context dependency remains unresolved and unprojected.
No stack object, response window, countering decision, or immediate-resolution operation is created.
rule.paraphrase: An activated mana ability resolves directly after activation rather than becoming a stack object. Stack-object targeting, countering, and responses therefore do not apply to that activation in the ordinary way.
rule.topic: Activated-mana immediate behavior without stack entry

limitations: The record does not define a general activation scheduler, reentrancy lock, or runtime event sequence.
rule.paraphrase: Beginning a mana-ability activation prevents another activation of that same ability until the first activation finishes resolving. This describes a narrow repeat-use constraint rather than a complete procedure scheduler.
rule.topic: The same mana ability cannot be repeated before resolution

limitations: The general triggered-ability subsystem remains unresolved; the exception is not trigger detection or execution.
rule.paraphrase: Triggered mana abilities rely on the ordinary triggered-ability rules while the selected child supplies their exceptional stack and resolution treatment.
rule.topic: Triggered-mana behavior retains a general trigger dependency

limitations: No trigger detection, immediate sequencing, response, stack, or priority operation is implemented.
The structurally owned source example is anchored as bytes only; no example prose or Card identity is retained.
rule.paraphrase: A qualifying mana trigger resolves directly after the mana ability responsible for it, without being placed on the stack or waiting for priority. It consequently has no ordinary stack-object targeting, countering, or response interaction.
rule.topic: Triggered-mana immediate sequencing without a priority wait

limitations: The numbered criteria range is represented by its two actual selected members.
Negative evidence is descriptive and does not supply a real classifier.
rule.paraphrase: An ability outside both selected criteria sets does not receive mana-ability classification. Spells are excluded from that category independently of their effects.
rule.topic: Failure of the criteria and spell identity exclude mana classification

limitations: No ordinary-ability numbered reference is invented where the selected block supplies none.
The negative trigger cases must be read with the complete selected triggered criteria; they do not remove its qualifying resolution or mana-added relationships.
No real target, event, potential output, or ordinary ability procedure is evaluated.
rule.paraphrase: The exclusions include an ability requiring a target, a potentially mana-producing trigger with an unsuitable triggering relationship, and a trigger tied to mana-ability activation that cannot generate mana. Excluded abilities continue to need the ordinary activated or triggered procedure appropriate to their kind.
rule.topic: Targeted and nonqualifying triggered abilities use ordinary procedures

limitations: Historical reference-data context is not ingested or retained as Card knowledge.
No real spell, Card text, casting behavior, or mana generation is interpreted.
rule.paraphrase: A spell retains spell classification even when resolving it could supply mana. Its casting and resolution therefore remain spell-procedure concerns, outside mana-ability classification and immediate-ability behavior.
rule.topic: Mana-producing spells remain spells rather than mana abilities

limitations: This frame assumes an activated ability and supplies no general recognizer.
Complete permission, timing, rollback and resolution semantics remain unresolved.
Ordinary stack context is subject to qualifying mana exceptions; no activation is performed.
rule.paraphrase: Activation has ordinary stack placement and cost context. Authority belongs to the source object's controller, falling back to its owner for an object without a controller, subject to an exception specified by that object. The listed procedure is ordered; failure to complete it has illegal-action and pre-activation recovery context. Completed declarations and payments are fixed.

limitations: No reveal, ability construction, controller evaluation or stack operation is supplied.
Qualifying mana abilities retain their independently proven exceptions.
The separate 109.4a attribution boundary does not require actual stack presence.
rule.paraphrase: The activator declares the ability. Use from a hidden zone carries card-reveal context. Ordinarily, the resulting ability is a noncard object at the top of the stack, carries the originating ability's text without other characteristics, and has the activator as controller. Its ordinary stack residence ends through countering, resolution or movement.
rule.topic: Activation announcement and ordinary ability-object context

limitations: This start-stage description does not establish that a particular proposal may begin or finish legally.
Both literal effect references remain unprojected; timing context supplies no effect-application machinery.
Stack entry during a proposal is distinct from the later point at which the spell becomes cast.
The activated-ability procedure's literal b-to-i import excludes this spell-start unit.
rule.paraphrase: A casting proposal begins with the player relocating the card or card copy to the top of the stack. Its associated characteristics and proposing-player control are described, together with stack-entry timing for specified characteristic changes and ability-granting effects. Residence ends through resolution, countering or another rule or effect moving the spell.
rule.topic: Casting proposal start, stack entry and initial effect timing

accepted: Proposed activated/triggered classifications within the documented retained-text scope.
Applicable criterion readings and method assessments.
Written costs, conditions, and output dependencies.
Conditional behavior conclusions supported by the existing evidence.
not_established: A general Card parser or automatic classifier.
Permission for source retention, redistribution, services, or AI export.
Approval of the earlier seven-subject pilot or any unrelated interpretation.
Resolution of changed text, gained abilities, copies, external effects, or arbitrary game states.
